title: supply-velocity-insights-gpu-sku-queue
summary: Working spreadsheet-style planning note that consolidates SKU mix velocity, regional lead times, and a prioritized procurement queue. Purpose: provide a lightweight operational runway for the next 6–12 months and a set of actionable reorder triggers for procurement and SRE. Not final; this is a snapshot used for weekly procurement sync.
content:
Context:
We are entering a volatile supply window (chip transition + end-of-life SKUs) while demand from Hosted API + Dedicated reservations shows a 18% QoQ growth trajectory. This sheet synthesizes SKU-level velocity (tokens/sec demand proxy), vendor lead-time distributions by region, and a prioritized order queue with suggested cadence and safety buffers.

Assumptions and signals used (source columns):
- Consumption proxy: effective GPU-hours derived from production token-hours and internal perf-ladders (higher for H100 quantized workloads).
- SKU universe: NVIDIA H100-80GB (h100-80), NVIDIA A100-80GB (a100-80), L40S (l40s-48), and smaller T4-equivalents for edge (t4-like).
- Vendor/region lead times: measured as median lead time from confirmed PO to delivery-ready in inventory (after staging + burn-in).
- Planned Dedicated launches: Q1/Q2 feature flags that add 2.5–3.5% incremental utilization per major tenant.
- Desired safety SLA on capacity: maintain a 4–6 week buffer for Hosted peak, 8–12 week buffer for Dedicated commitments.

Key heuristics and formulas included in sheet:
- Reorder point (units): ROP = D_avg * LT_med + SafetyStock
  - D_avg: rolling 28-day average GPU-days demand for that SKU in the target region
  - LT_med: median lead time (days) for vendor+region
  - SafetyStock = z * sigma_d * sqrt(LT_med), z chosen by criticality (1.0 default for hosted, 1.65 for enterprise committed capacity)
- Order cadence suggestion: prefer monthly smaller tranches for high-variance lead-time SKUs (H100), quarterly bulk orders for stable A100 supply to secure pricing discounts.

Inventory snapshot (CSV table columns: region, sku, in_stock_units, allocated_reserved, available_free, 28d_avg_daily_demand, median_lt_days, suggested_rop, suggested_order_qty):
us-west,h100-80,32,20,12,0.85,72,61,50
us-east,a100-80,120,40,80,1.20,42,52,100
eu-west,l40s-48,40,10,30,0.30,35,11,20
apac-sg,a100-80,24,6,18,0.95,60,57,40
us-central,t4-like,200,60,140,0.40,21,9,0

Priority queue logic (short text):
1) Critical replenishment: SKUs where available_free < 2 * 28d_avg_daily_demand OR allocated_reserved exceeds 65% of in_stock. Trigger immediate PO with expedited shipping where vendor lead times > 45 days.
2) Capacity smoothing: If median_lt_days is high (>50) but utilization growth is steady, schedule laddered orders (3 tranches, 30-day spacing).
3) Opportunistic hedging: For A100 and equivalent models where price discounts are >8% for >100-unit tranches, negotiate quarterly bulk + staggered delivery to mitigate lead-time risk.

Regional lead-time observations (bulleted):
- APAC (Singapore) shows longest variance for H100 due to customs + limited freight corridors: median 60 days, 90th percentile 110 days.
- US-West has fastest turnaround for A100 (median ~30–42 days) when using two preferred distributors; H100 still slower due to allocation caps.
- EU-West shows consistent parity with US-East for L40S shipments but additional VAT import lag typically adds 7–10 days on average.

Procurement pipeline (open POs and suggested actions):
- PO#7861 (vendor-X) - H100-80 x 60 units - expected delivery window: 2025-03-10 to 2025-03-20 - action: confirm partial early ship for 20 units, request staging center in us-west.
- PO#7899 (vendor-Y) - A100-80 x 200 units - expected: 2025-06 (bulk) - action: request split shipments (50/75/75) to hit Q2 launch needs and reduce single-point inventory pressure.
- PO#7922 (regional broker) - L40S x 30 units - expected: 2025-01-30 - done; arrange SRE burn-in slot week of 2025-02-05.

Cost and accounting notes (short):
- Unit economics used here are net landed cost (unit + freight + import + staging). For H100 we've assumed $18k/unit landed for budgeting; for A100 $9.2k/unit landed; L40S $4.5k/unit. These are placeholders pending final vendor quotes.

Risks and mitigations (bullet list):
- Risk: Single-vendor allocation limits cause slower fill rates. Mitigation: multi-vendor split, maintain 10–15% active secondary vendor pipeline.
- Risk: Demand spike from unforecasted enterprise trial. Mitigation: carve small urgent pool (10 units) per region as emergency reserve; convert from dedicated buffer if needed.
- Risk: Currency / tariff shock. Mitigation: negotiate partial currency indexing in contracts or use hedging for large tranches.

Open questions for procurement sync (TODOs):
- Confirm whether finance will accept staged invoices for split shipments to smooth cashflow.
- Should we increase z (safety multiplier) for APAC H100 to 2.0 given high lead-time variance?
- Which distributors are certificate-approved for EU VAT fast-track import (need list from legal).

Action items (tracked):
- [ ] Procurement: escalate PO#7861 for early partial ship (owner: Asha)
- [ ] SRE: reserve burn-in capacity for incoming L40S batch (owner: Leila)
- [ ] Finance: review landed cost assumptions and confirm budget band for H100 (owner: Miguel)
- [ ] Eng infra: run a 28-day simulation on utilization after splitting PO#7899 (owner: Riley)

Notes to self / rough margin calculations:
- If we convert 20 H100 units to dedicated-only nodes with avg 65% utilization at 3.2x effective token throughput relative to A100, incremental revenue coverage per unit improves payback from 7.2 months -> ~5.1 months (very rough). Need finance model to formalize.

Versioning and provenance:
- This sheet borrows demand proxies from analytics pipeline (query id: analytics:gpu_demand_rollup_v3) and vendor LT signals from procurement tracker (procure:leadtime-history-v2). Reconcile those two sources before finalizing PO sizes.

Meeting cadence:
- Weekly procurement sync (Tue 10am PT) — use this doc as the running agenda; append PO status and update the CSV snapshot row counts each week.
